The project

Finding a new place for analogue writing.

ORG Verlag is a Berlin-based maker of ring-binder organisers and calendars, with an emphasis on craftsmanship, refillability and long-term use. The SRH Lab project explored how to communicate those existing qualities to new audiences through positioning, content and a digital concept.

Audience

Connecting with a new generation.

The strategy moved beyond age alone to consider shared values, motivations and ways of using analogue products. Three audience groups gave the communication plan its direction.

01

Digital Detox Professionals

People looking for focus, fewer digital distractions and a durable organisational system.

02

Young Creators

Creative students, designers and illustrators using paper for self-expression, with an interest in customisation and paper quality.

03

Gift Givers

People looking for meaningful, well-made gifts, personalisation and a straightforward buying experience.

Positioning

Making analogue feel relevant again.

Offline is luxury.

The proposed direction positions the ring-book as a personal space for organising, creating and reflecting. Craftsmanship, refillable systems and customisation connect the traditional product with contemporary routines. The aim was to make those qualities visible while keeping the brand’s character.

Visual direction

Warm, tactile and intentionally analogue.

The documented visual direction combines warmth, structure and a professional feel. Product photography, paper, materials and everyday settings bring the physical character of the ring-book into the digital experience.

Content strategy

Turning the idea into communication.

The marketing plan proposes several connected ways to introduce the brand and show how its products could fit into daily life. These are strategic recommendations, rather than a launched campaign.

01

Show the people and craft

Use brand stories, production and behind-the-scenes content to make the family business and the work behind each product visible.

02

Make focused routines tangible

Planning sessions, offline morning routines and desk setups show how an analogue system can fit into a working day.

03

Invite creative expression

Journaling, decorating and sketching content connects the product with the interests of young creators.

04

Collaborate with relevant communities

The proposal includes smaller creators, artists and cultural partners, selected for audience fit and shared values.

What the brand could talk about.

The proposed posting plan alternates About us, Facts, Young Creators and Detox Professionals. The content recommendations translate those categories into practical formats.

Brand & craft

About us / Facts

Behind the brand, craftsmanship, product details and answers to community questions.

Instagram · TikTok

Young Creators

Plan with me, journal with me, decorating, writing ASMR and stationery routines.

Instagram · TikTok · LinkedIn

Detox Professionals

Offline morning routines, focused work sessions, planning tips and digital-versus-analogue reflections.

Digital concept

Giving the strategy a digital home.

The website concept brings the project’s positioning into a digital environment, combining editorial storytelling, product presentation and the tactile character of analogue writing.

From positioning to experience.

01

Craftsmanship → brand story

The strategy’s emphasis on making and heritage appears in the concept’s Made in Germany message and imagery of materials and production.

02

Long-term use → refillability

The refillable-system proposition is made visible in the concept’s product messaging and refill section.

03

Digital detox → editorial tone

The proposal’s Offline is luxury direction becomes a calm visual world and language about writing, focus and time away from screens.

Reflection

What I took from it.

This project pushed me to think beyond the appearance of a brand and consider how positioning, content and digital design work together. Starting with the audience and communication strategy gave the final concept a clearer direction and helped me see the website as one part of a wider brand experience.
